Not every kid wants to write a paragraph 🙌

Try the 3-Option Choice Board. They can sketch, speak, or write to show what they learned.

Same goal. More voice.
https://youtu.be/3j4OC1Ya1lA
#ChoiceBoards #UDL

Picture a second grader. They're sketching a fox in a forest 🦊

That's the Knowledge Journal. Kids draw, label, and tell the story of what they're learning about animals and habitats.

Science meets writing meets wonder.
https://youtu.be/0fli_6niKOU
#Science #ElementaryTeachers

Prediction Pop is the warm-up your kids will ask for 🍿

Show one image. They guess what comes next.

Then read. Then check. Their predictions get sharper every time.
https://youtu.be/_MswxTESzko
#ReadingStrategies #BellRinger

Same idea. Three formats. One simple template 📋

Show What You Know: 3 Ways lets kids prove they got it through writing, talking, or making something.

It's quick. It's fair. It's a keeper.
https://youtu.be/2rjatO-5mp0
#FormativeAssessment #UDL

Some kids freeze the second a task starts. That's not laziness 🧠

The Task Initiation Toolkit gives them small steps to get going. Choose. Plan. Start. Check.

Save this one. You'll use it more than you think.
https://youtu.be/VdlhUJGBJoQ
#ExecutiveFunction #SEL

Tell me your summer in 6 words.

That's it. No more, no fewer.

Kids will groan, then grin, then write the best line of the day.

Use it on day one 🌞

https://youtu.be/wzJOMRz6Uy0

Three little words can stretch any sentence 🧩

Because. But. So. That's it.

Have kids expand a basic sentence using each one. They start writing with reasons, contrasts, and effects without even knowing it.
https://youtu.be/HlSP7pK982I
#WritingStrategies #ELA

Want kids hyped about evidence? Make it a race 🏃

Evidence Relay Race splits the room into teams. Each kid finds a quote, runs it to the next teammate, and the team builds the strongest claim.

Loud, fast, and packed with thinking.
https://youtu.be/ptHpp2IPFtA
#TeacherStrategies #ELA

column3: PLC Data Dive Prep  —  Activity Sheet
column7:
PLC meetings hit different when you walk in ready 📊

The PLC Data Dive Prep sheet gives you a clean place to log trends, name the gap, and pick one move you want to try next.

Walk in sharp. Walk out with a plan.
https://youtu.be/ictYj6aoB3s
#PLC #TeacherLeadership

Silent. Quick. Powerful. That's Chalk Talk 🖍️

Post a question on chart paper. Hand out markers. Let kids write, draw, and respond to each other without saying a word.

You'll be amazed at what comes out.
https://youtu.be/nen8xCC6Hk0
#ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines

There's a stranger in the room today. It's the mystery text 🕵️

Kids read clues, take notes, and crack the case. By the end, they've done a close read without knowing it.

That's the magic of Mystery Text Detective.
https://youtu.be/HSrfcojfu7c
#ELA #ReadingStrategies

Three quick steps. Big payoff 🎧

Stop. Look. Listen. That's the whole routine.

Kids slow down, take in what's around them, and notice what they'd skip on a normal day. Use it before reading, before talking, or at the start of class.
https://youtu.be/vs0SNGxHGxE
#ProjectZero #Mindfulness

Two pictures. One question. Hours of thinking 🪞

Same and Different is the routine that makes kids slow down and notice. They list what's alike, what's not, and why it matters.

Works for any subject.
https://youtu.be/6C4a144v6-s
#ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines

Every system has three layers: the parts, the people, and how they work together.

This Project Zero routine helps kids map any system. From a bee hive to a school, the same lens works.

Save this one for your next big unit! 🐝

Watch: https://youtu.be/XI4oDKn9hxI

#ProjectZero #SystemsThinking #TeachingStrategies

Got a heavy text or a busy lesson? Use the Info Organizer 🗂️

It gives kids a clean spot for the main idea, the details that back it up, and the questions they still have.

Less mess, more learning.
https://youtu.be/HVuMacNO7KY
#GraphicOrganizers #TeacherTools

Most class debates fall flat.

Tug for Truth fixes that. Kids place each fact on a tug-of-war rope, pulling toward 'true' or 'false.' They have to defend each pull.

Watch the room come alive! 💥

Watch: https://youtu.be/DfGprA3DK9Q

#ProjectZero #CriticalThinking #Debate

Need an idea, a problem, or a plan? Try Compass Points 🧭

Kids name what Excites them, what Worries them, what they Need to know, and what they Suggest.

Four prompts. Real talk. Tons of buy-in.
https://youtu.be/CG8A0fyTAzg
#ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines

One book. Twelve takes.

Circle of Viewpoints asks each student to read a scene through a different character's eyes. Same words, brand new meaning.

Try it with any text and watch them light up! 📖

Watch: https://youtu.be/tELh8qbUwzs

#ProjectZero #Reading #Discussion

Reading checks don't have to be boring 🎨

Color Symbol Image asks kids to pick a color, a symbol, and an image that show what a text means to them.

Three small choices. Wild deep thinking.
https://youtu.be/EvakG6ZOcKM
#TeacherStrategies #VisualLearning

Today, we're not just reading. We're solving cases 🔍

Context Clue Detectives turns hard words into mysteries. Kids hunt for hints around the word, then pitch their best guess.

Reading gets fun fast.
https://youtu.be/kmIn8TIZAMA
#ReadingStrategies #Vocabulary

Want kids to actually listen to each other? Try the Perspective Swap Challenge 👥

They argue one side. Then they swap and argue the other.

Not just debate. It's empathy in action.
https://youtu.be/1Y9dFMmi9rI
#TeacherStrategies #SEL

What if your math class moved into a tiny house? 🏠

Kids design a 200 square foot home, work the math, and make the trade-offs real. Area, ratios, budget. All baked in.

It's the kind of project where kids stop asking when they'll use this stuff.

Peek at how it plays!
https://youtu.be/EQJDYqDtUx8

Writing block? Hand kids a Choice Board 📝

Nine prompts. They pick three. Boom, they're writing.

It's the easiest way to keep voice and choice in your room without losing the goal.
https://youtu.be/KQi8vac-Tz4
#WritingStrategies #ChoiceBoards

No talking. Just markers.

Chalk Talk Mix is a Project Zero routine where kids write their thoughts on big paper and reply to each other in silence. The room gets loud in a quiet way.

It pulls voices that never raise a hand! ✏️

Watch: https://youtu.be/WCFXilI4ba4

#ProjectZero #StudentVoice #ClassroomRoutines

Picture a gym, but for grammar.

Grammar Circuit Training sets up stations that hit one rule each. Commas at one stop. Subject-verb at the next. Kids rotate and get reps.

Way more fun than a worksheet! 💪

Watch: https://youtu.be/KIRUv8KA3zg

#Grammar #ELA #TeacherTips

Check out Curiosity Explorer. This video guides you through a smart way to ask questions and really think things through. You'll see what you don't know yet and learn how to use that to grow. Great for anyone who wants to boost their learning skills! 🎬

What if your students could chat with George Washington and Rosa Parks at the same time?

History Mix-Up sets up that exact scene. Kids ask one question and watch each figure answer in their own voice.

Time travel for the classroom! ⏳

Watch: https://youtu.be/LDBKj132UH0

#History #SocialStudies #SchoolAIhttps://youtu.be/lanOI-EPj2s
G2318

Four words can change the whole vibe of class:

'What makes you say that?'

It's a Project Zero routine that pushes kids to back up what they think. No bossy tone needed.

Use it once and you'll keep using it! 🤔

Watch: https://youtu.be/bNNSCEoHoqI

#Discussion #StudentVoice #ProjectZero

Graffiti has a place in your classroom. I'll wait.

Graffiti or Gallery? lets kids tag big paper with their thoughts on a topic, then walk around to read what others wrote.

Loud, messy, and stuck in their heads! 🎨

Watch: https://youtu.be/Q40PbZ8V60g

#ClassroomIdeas #ActiveLearning #TeacherTips

i-Ready scores tell you what kids missed. They don't tell you why.

The Why Check space asks each student a quick set of follow-ups so you can see if it was speed, focus, or a real gap.

Way more useful than the score alone! 📊

Watch: https://youtu.be/W99JObSVjt0

#iReady #DataDriven #TeacherLife

Kids think books are sealed truth. They're not.

Question the Author teaches readers to push back at the page: why did the writer pick this word, this scene, this ending?

Once they start, they don't stop! 📚

Watch: https://youtu.be/405Ejctt-ds

#Reading #ReadingTeacher #SchoolAI

Most kids skip the 'why' on a math problem.

Why Did This Happen? flips that. Kids run the steps in reverse and figure out the cause behind each move.

It builds the kind of thinking that sticks for tests! 🧠

Watch: https://youtu.be/MnjUC7Q3xMU

#MathTeacher #CriticalThinking #SchoolAI

Some lessons want students to know stuff. The best ones want them to care.

Think, Feel, Care is a Project Zero routine that asks kids to step into a person's shoes and look at the world from their side.

It builds heart and brain at once! ❤️

Watch: https://youtu.be/FnjF6OWA0zo

#SEL #ProjectZero #Empathy

column3: I Used to Think... Now I Think...
column7:
The best 5 minutes of class might be the last 5.

Try this Project Zero routine: I Used to Think... Now I Think... Kids name what shifted in their brain during the lesson.

It works for any topic, K through 12! 💡

Watch: https://youtu.be/PMQcW3CMIDY

#ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines #TeacherTips

Vocab lists are fine. Vocab webs are better.

Word Why Web links each word to a reason, an image, and a use. Kids build the web together and the words really stick.

Try it once and your tier 2 words will pop! 🕸️

Watch: https://youtu.be/ZhAYSw2o3i0

#Vocab #ReadingTeacher #SchoolAI

column3: How Do We Know Students Are Learning?
column7:
Voice levels feel old until you turn them into a game.

Tic Tac Toe with voice levels gives kids a fun way to track their own noise.

Three in a row earns a class win.

Easy, low-prep, big payoff 🎯

https://youtu.be/WjpzdWcyM3Y

Bees do not get enough credit.

Pollination Station drops kids into the role of a bee and asks them to spread pollen, dodge bugs, and keep the garden alive.

Science class, but make it a buzz! 🐝

Watch: https://youtu.be/-nrPjjIWrWU

#ScienceTeacher #LifeScience #SchoolAI

History textbooks make feudal life sound flat. It wasn't.

Feudal Ladder lets kids climb (or fall) the social ranks of the Middle Ages. They take on a role and feel the rules from inside.

Way better than a worksheet! 🏰

Watch: https://youtu.be/eGT5_JWjvSs

#SocialStudies #History #SchoolAI

Kids miss the moral?

Drop them into Fable Moral Detector. They read short fables, hunt for the lesson, and lock in their guess before the reveal. Quick win for ELA warm-ups 🐢

Try it: https://youtu.be/rPPoWlXYEA0

Most kids freeze when you ask them what makes a poem feel a certain way.

Poetic Craft Decoder breaks craft into bite-size moves like sound, line breaks, and word choice. Kids tag what the poet did, then say why it works 🪶

Built for close reading: https://youtu.be/gG5VJGIHsx0

Most kids skip the middle of a story when they retell it.

Story Retelling Space holds them to all five parts. Setting, problem, events, solution, and ending. Kids type it out, AI gently nudges what's missing, and they revise on the spot.

Built for guided practice 📖

See it work: https://youtu.be/XdCd8Ewn1sI

Most kids think every story has one moral.

Moral Match-Up shows them three takes on the same fable and asks which fits best. They defend the pick with text proof. Way better than a multiple choice quiz 🎯

Try it: https://youtu.be/wW5g7aK_zqE

Most lessons on 1776 skip the part where neighbors fought neighbors.

Patriot Perspective Coach has kids step into a loyalist's shoes and a patriot's. Same town, same year, two very different views. Empathy meets history 🇺🇸

Watch it: https://youtu.be/aMIJQvDgJkk

One concept. Three ways to show you get it.
Write it. Draw it. Teach it to a friend.
Because the best way to know if your students really understand something? Watch them explain it three different ways. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=az0j9MdgDkw

One symbol can hold a whole story.

Symbol Gallery asks kids to walk through a museum of icons, then explain what each one means and why it matters.

Great for lit, history, art class, you name it! 🎨

Watch: https://youtu.be/6s8g1KGZZSc

#TeachingStrategies #Reading #SocialStudies

Pick a fable. Draw the beginning, middle, and end. Tell it back in your own words.
Retelling is how kids prove they got the story. This one makes it feel like play. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HQpUm-bIsiQ

Picture this. A note slid under your door says 'meet at the oak at noon.'

That's the kind of hook in Mystery Clue Investigator. Kids gather clues, weigh suspects, and crack the case. Reading skills with built-in fun 🔍

Sleuth here: https://youtu.be/LkWne-fzrN0

Reading 'Inside Out and Back Again' this month?

Ha's Journey Tracker keeps a map of where she's been and how she feels at each stop. Kids follow the heart-strings of a refugee story without losing the plot 🗺️

See it in action: https://youtu.be/hRiRYFjEjZA

Save this for poetry units 📝

Poetry Element Spotter pulls up a real poem and asks kids to point to the rhyme, the meter, the metaphor. They tag what they see, AI checks their hunches, and they level up fast.

Watch it: https://youtu.be/Ev88VEQHe-s

Save this one for descriptive writing 🦁

Five Senses Safari pulls kids into a setting and asks what do you see, hear, smell, touch, and taste. They build sensory detail without staring at a blank page.

Watch the safari: https://youtu.be/MDnrQZmwI44

Stella's a star who lives just past the moon. She loves to chat with kids about space.

Try her out for a quick spark before your next space lesson. Kids ask the questions, she shares fun space facts, and you get five free minutes to set up your room 🌟

Watch the demo here: https://youtu.be/ps4UYFmrKek

Story arc trips up most middle schoolers.

Narrative Structure Lab walks them through hook, rising action, climax, and falling action. They label each beat, then test it on their own draft. Big upgrade for writing units ✏️

See the lab: https://youtu.be/w67uzKmA964

Tattling kills your flow as a teacher.

Meet Mr. Tattle. He's an AI that hears the small stuff so you can teach. Kids type it up, get a calm reply, and move on.

The classroom mood shifts fast! 😌

Watch: https://youtu.be/BoKixGgtV04

#ClassroomManagement #TeacherLife #SchoolAI

Teaching habitats this week?

Hank the helper knows every nook and biome. Kids quiz him about polar caps, deserts, ponds, you name it. He keeps it kid-safe and fun.

Free way to spice up science 🦦

See Hank in action: https://youtu.be/qYt5IOmgA0o

Want a closing routine that sticks?

Reflection Postcard. Kids write a quick note to next week's self about what they learned today. Two minutes, big payoff for memory.

Bookmark this for Friday wrap-ups 📮

Watch the demo: https://youtu.be/S9AaR5mF-H4

Want a vocab tool your kids will beg to use?

Vocabulary Voyage turns word study into a quick game. Kids tap AI for word clues, kid-friendly examples, and a check at the end so you know they got it.

Save this for your next word list 📚

Watch it work: https://youtu.be/QeZB3_e9sig

Want kids to really remember the bones of the body?

Skeleton Defender turns the body into a game. Each round asks them to defend a part by naming it and showing how it works.

It's review with a pulse! 💀

Watch: https://youtu.be/Fyyakbr_3zg

#ScienceClass #BodySystems #SchoolAI

Want kids to think deeper without the lecture?

The Explanation Game from Project Zero asks one prompt, then digs three layers down with why, why, why. Kids start to notice they have more to say than they first thought 💡

Try the routine: https://youtu.be/uB1OIE_HCVE

What if Anansi got caught?

Trickster Tale Talk lets kids interview tricksters from around the world and ask the hard questions. Why the tricks? What did you learn? Quick read, big payoff 🕷️

Listen in: https://youtu.be/JSlkTdnx3HA

What if Frankenstein's creature could speak for himself?

In this Space, kids step into the monster's shoes and tell the world what it felt like to be cast out. Empathy, voice, and theme all in one Space 💭

Hear the creature: https://youtu.be/Rc_mijTsVTw

What if your students could feel like a rock?

The Rock Cycle Journey turns earth science into a story. Kids move through each stage and tell the tale from the rock's point of view.

It's silly, sure, but the science sticks! 🪨

Watch: https://youtu.be/ncgJZwg1A50

#ScienceTeacher #EarthScience #SchoolAI

Why teach ethics in science class?

Because the kids running tomorrow's labs need to think hard about right and wrong now. This Space puts them in the judge seat. They weigh the case, hear the facts, and decide ⚖️

Try the Tribunal: https://youtu.be/qzyzV3MMB4s

You're a trader in 850 AD. You set out from Xi'an with silk, headed for Baghdad.

That's the spark behind Silk Road Trader. Kids haggle, swap stories with locals, and learn how trade shaped the world. Way more fun than a worksheet 🐪

Watch the journey: https://youtu.be/2qBKVu8ZDdQ

Your next science lesson could feel like a NASA mission.

Space Explorer drops kids into a fake mission and asks them to make smart calls along the way. Think Oregon Trail but for space!

The wonder is built in. 🚀

Watch: https://youtu.be/jstCQGulRTs

#ScienceClass #StudentEngagement #EdTech

Your students just met Bonnie.
She has questions about her brain, heart, lungs, and muscles.
They have answers (and a reflection corner to prove it).
Science class just got a personal tutor. Try it →
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E1cnEZpD7No

"I don't get it" is hard to act on.
"Here's the exact part that's fuzzy, sketched out, with an arrow" is gold.
Give your students a way to show you where they're stuck. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=34q327Gt9UE

Fill in K and W before your @getSchoolAI session.
Fill in L after.
That one small shift turns a chat into a learning loop students can actually see.
Low lift, high payoff. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5kNeI6SrurY

Romeo vs. Mercutio isn't just a compare activity.
It's a T-chart that builds a thesis.
Students pull evidence, spot the contrast, and write a claim that actually means something.
Shakespeare who? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FHnUIwnwJRc

Round 1: Kids list 10 things they see.
Round 2: Look again. Find 10 MORE.
That second round is where the magic happens. Close observation becomes a habit, not a one-time ask. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wflj8VUfIpc

Same ideas, two ways to capture them.
That's personalized learning in one screen. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KQv1Qk2KcQE

Same topic. Three paragraph types. Five minutes each.
Narrative. Opinion. Informational.
Your writers will feel the shift in their brains when the mode changes. That's the whole point. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z44eQfR-Hso

Sort it. Define it. Promise it.
This Space turns a science concept into something students can actually act on today.
The "My Earth Promise" line at the bottom? Chef's kiss. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vXGhUtQH2Q

What do I do first? What comes next? Am I done?
Students who struggle with tasks don't need more reminders.
They need a plan they built themselves.
This Space does exactly that. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhIiTKMpwRU

Word banks. Sentence frames. Text evidence.
This Space meets every reader where they are and still gets them to the same finish line.
That's the goal every time. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mtBi5WF_Ts0

Your students don't just read a character.
They sketch them, label them, and find the moments words can't catch.Dual coding meets close reading and it hits different.Try it → https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ABgXFiMWuwM

column3: 3 Checks for Under­stand­ing That Actually Work
column7:
Most exit tickets just ask 'did you get it?' Spoiler. Kids say yes either way.

These three quick checks pull real proof of learning instead. Save this if you want fast, honest feedback that helps you plan day two 📈

Watch it: https://youtu.be/Gc_XJ1m4mYE

Teaching loneliness as a theme this month?

Isolation Theme Mapper helps kids spot the moments a character feels cut off and trace what leads up to those scenes. Frankenstein, Hamlet, even The Giver, it works for all of them 💭

Try it: https://youtu.be/wyNfgg3m-WI

You know the ghost is in the closet. The kid in the story does not.

That tiny gap is dramatic irony. Detective puts kids on the case. They find moments where readers know more than the characters and write up the why. Hidden hook in lots of stories 🕵️

See it: https://youtu.be/TTvbdYag02E

Kids forget the planet order every year. Same struggle, every grade.

Planet Order Explorer turns it into a quick game. Drag the planets in line, get a quirky fact about each, and lock the order in. Sun to Pluto, sorted in five 🪐

Watch it: https://youtu.be/DWpiDJdbrdY

Looking for a habitat lesson that runs itself? Habitat Match-Up is your go-to. Kids match plants and animals to their home, talk it out, and learn fast. Save it for your next CKLA science day 🌎 https://youtu.be/5vfFXnv4hCc #CKLA #Science #TeacherLife

column3: Where in the World Are You?
column7:
Most map lessons fall flat because the place feels far away.

Where in the World Are You? drops kids in the spot, gives them a few clues, and asks them to figure out where they are. Maps, weather, and culture, all in one mini Space 🌍

Try it: https://youtu.be/3UuSDfdYlTg

Need a fast way to lock in body systems with your CKLA kids? This sorting game does it in under 10 minutes. Drag, drop, debate, repeat. The kind of review they really ask to do again 🫀 https://youtu.be/bgLdaAj-2Kc #CKLA #Science #LearningGames

Note-taking that sticks isn't pretty handwriting.

It's three moves. Sketch, summary, and a question for tomorrow. Try this routine for one week and watch retention jump.

Full demo here 📝 https://youtu.be/GDJb5Jr2ku8

One of my second graders looked at a beetle and said, Wait, that's not an insect? Cue the giggles. Bug Body Detective lets kids ask the bug itself and figure it out. CKLA learning that feels like a game 🐛 https://youtu.be/_5DyeNpUkNk #CKLA #Science #EdTech

column3: Peel the Fruit: Layers of Meaning
column7:
Peel the Fruit is one of my favorite Project Zero routines.

Start with the skin, what you see on the surface. Slice deeper, what's hiding under the words. Get to the seed, what does it really mean? Kids think harder without you saying a thing 🍑

Watch the routine: https://youtu.be/FRCOka9QbsU

Save this for peer feedback days 💬

Feedback Sentence Starters gives kids the words they need so 'good job' becomes 'I notice you used a hook to pull me in.' Better feedback in five minutes flat.

See it: https://youtu.be/Tc5tqmUlIk0

Save this for writing centers 🧩

Paragraph Parts Puzzle drops a topic sentence, three details, and a closer in a jumbled stack. Kids drag them in order and explain why. Quick, no-prep, and they leave the mat with the parts in their head.

Watch it: https://youtu.be/KYlky70OnSY

Teaching myths and need to skip the prep spiral? The Myth Lesson Finder pulls the lesson, the hook, and talking points in one go. CKLA teachers, save this. Your Sunday self will thank you 📚 https://youtu.be/KzHvfYQIT-g #CKLA #ELA #TeacherHack

Three hashtags. One mystery story. Go.

Hanging Hashtags is a quick warm-up where kids label a story they just read with three smart tags and back each up with text proof. Done in five flat 🏷️

Watch it: https://youtu.be/fhaBDrgP_Lc

Two characters walk into the same scene and see two different things.

Same and Different Detective puts kids on the case. They spot what's alike, name what's not, and learn how point of view shapes a story 🔎

See the case: https://youtu.be/Z0vYLTdNX_s

What do you think about this topic?
How does it make you feel?
What do you care about most?
Three questions that turn any lesson into something your students actually want to talk about. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=syd7bKkBCKM

What if your kids could chat with a trail guide who knew every tree, animal, and trick of the woods? That's the magic of Trail Guide Talk. CKLA reading just got a whole lot more fun 🌲 https://youtu.be/o6d2Wnx_HRo #CKLA #ReadingForFun #EdTech

column3: Every Brain Has Its Own Superpower
column7: What if different learner wasn't a label but a clue? Every brain has its own edge. Once you spot it, lessons start clicking in ways you didn't plan for. This blended setup helps you find each kid's strengths fast 🧠 https://youtu.be/eCclny2PnNo #BlendedLearning #UDL #StudentVoice

column3: FROM FLAT LESSONS TO REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS
column7:
Here's a hot take. Kids don't tune out because the topic is dull.
They tune out when it has no link to real life. Fix that one thing and the room wakes up!
This talk shows how to turn flat notes into stuff kids can really chew on.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MbTiy1CCE_M
Small shift, big change 💡
Ever feel like your room runs you, not the other way? This session breaks down real steps to bring calm back.

My students used to dread giving talks. Then we tried a Presentation Party. Snacks. Cheers. A real crowd. Soon the shyest kid was beaming. Try it once and your room won't feel the same 🎉 https://youtu.be/RVyRcDuf03E #TeacherLife #StudentVoice #EdTech
Save this one for the first week of school or the day before a big break.
Small tweaks here make a huge lift. Worth a watch! 🙌

Some weeks the room runs you instead of the other way around. We've all been there. The Control the Chaos Bundle is the toolkit I wish I'd had on my hardest days. Quick wins, simple moves, and calm that really lasts 🙌 https://youtu.be/bDzQER2q9pY #ClassroomManagement #TeacherLife

Want kids to give a speech that doesn't put the class to sleep? Use the How To frame. Pick a topic they love. Show the steps. Add one prop. That's it. Save this for your next speaking unit 🎤 https://youtu.be/Ff9VMjGL_rU #PublicSpeaking #ELA #TeacherTips

Want kids to think deeper without doing all the work? Here's a fast trick that gets them building inner thinking in minutes. The Inner Thinking Builder turns CKLA reading into real aha moments. Quick, fun, and it really sticks 💡 https://youtu.be/Quo35FaCdXU #CKLA #ReadingHelp #EdTech

column3: Wonder Wheel: Drive Your Own Discovery
column7:
What if wonder had a steering wheel?

That's the whole idea behind the Wonder Wheel. Kids spin into questions they really want to answer 🎡

It turns "I don't know what to write about" into "I have too many ideas to choose from."

See it spin here: https://youtu.be/qEKcrapkVnY

Use it Monday and watch their notebooks fill up!

column3: Ladder of Feedback — climb in order
column7:
Bad feedback can wreck a project. The Ladder of Feedback fixes that. 🪜

Climb in order. First, clarify. Then value. Then state concerns. Last, suggest. Skipping steps is where tone breaks down.

Try it with your students before peer reviews. It saves you so much repair work later.

Watch it in action: https://youtu.be/EzQzck-G8Dc

Crazy 8s isn't a drawing exercise. That's the trick.

Eight ideas in eight minutes. One sheet of paper folded into eight squares. Pencils only ✏️

Kids stop second-guessing. The bad ideas get out of the way and the strange ones start to shine.

Watch the sprint in action: https://youtu.be/Fb2FRevQa5E

Their twentieth idea is always better than their first!

Color isn't just a vibe. It's a writing prompt. 🎨

Color Story Studio asks kids to pick a shade and tell its story. Where does it live? What does it feel? Who shows up around it?

The results are wild in the best way. Quiet kids find their voice fast.

Take a look: https://youtu.be/I6Gq_CmyVZg

Eight ideas in eight minutes. That's Crazy 8's. ⏱️

Fold a paper into eight squares. Set a timer. Sketch one idea per square. Don't stop, don't filter, don't rank yet.

The "bad" ideas crack the door open for the great ones. I use this any time a class gets stuck.

Try it: https://youtu.be/OUsb9xgcHM4

Most students freeze when you say "draft."

Try a storyboard first. Six boxes, six moments. They sketch and scribble before they write a word. ✏️

It pulls the pressure off the page and turns plot into a path you can see.

Watch the move: https://youtu.be/1Bm6tn-zaZk

Got a wall of sticky notes after a brainstorm?

Saturate and Group is your next move. Spread them all out so the whole team can see, then sort them into themes. Patterns pop fast. 🧠

It's a quiet step that shifts a messy pile into clear next steps.

See how it works: https://youtu.be/SbHg3ujom24

Picture this. A 5th grader writing as a passenger on the Titanic, choosing what to pack, what to leave, and who to find first.

That's the power of a POV writing task. It turns a fact list into a felt moment. ⚓

Kids stop summing up and start living it. They write longer, deeper, and with way more heart.

Watch how it unfolds: https://youtu.be/QL7nvHWfYT8

Teaching the War of 1812 can feel dry.

But there's a way to bring it to life so kids really care. Maps, voices, and the moments that flipped the story change the whole game. 📜

I love how this CKLA unit lets students step into the time and ask big questions.

Take a peek: https://youtu.be/_jL9h_aq0oE

Teaching kids to spot fake sources?

Try the Source Stoplight. 🚦 Red means stop and check. Yellow means slow down and ask why. Green means it checks out.

It's simple enough for a 4th grader and sharp enough for high school.

Watch the move: https://youtu.be/IB4dhl3pnHw

Storyboards aren't just for movies. 🎬

They're a design thinking tool that helps kids picture each step before they build. It saves so much time later.

Try it next time you brief a project. Watch how the room shifts.

See it in action: https://youtu.be/iHk86IC1HfI

Want kids to really get how a user feels?

A Journey Map breaks down what someone sees, thinks, and does at each step. It turns flat ideas into rich stories. 🗺️

I love this one before students pitch a fix. They build real care first.

Watch the quick how-to: https://youtu.be/xd7oAzJ4vxU

A teacher came to me stuck. Her kids could name a problem but couldn't say why it mattered.

We tried a Point of View Madlib. They filled in the blanks. User. Need. Insight 💡

Their problem statements went from flat to focused in one round.

Watch how it works: https://youtu.be/nZAok-VAudk

Steal it for your next project!

Mystery + ELA = Murdoku 🕵️

Kids piece together clues, build their case, and use what they read to solve the puzzle.

It's a fresh way to teach close reading without the groans. Such a fun review tool for any unit! #ELA #ReadingSkills #ClassroomFun https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDU4OCpqqQw

Save this one for your next writing unit.

The 3 Voice Draft asks kids to write the same paragraph three ways. Casual. Formal. Persuasive ✏️

Same content, three voices. They start to feel how word choice changes the room.

Quick demo here: https://youtu.be/mjOuMwliZYc

Bookmark it for revision week!

Your students are using AI. The question is whether they know how it works.

I made a quick lab that walks teachers through how to teach kids what AI is good at, where it slips up, and when to trust it 🧠

See it here: https://youtu.be/gQcnOPAnx24

Try it with your team and tell me what your kids notice. Their questions are wild in the best way!

How do you make sure your design works for all kids? 🔍 Talk to extreme users.

The d.school's Extreme Users tool pushes them to learn from folks at the edges, where the best ideas often hide.

It sparks fresh thinking on every project! #DesignThinking #UserResearch #FreshIdeas https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bqqaJfrAUAI

Stuck in a brainstorm rut? 🚫 Try the Worst Possible Idea.

It's a d.school trick that gets kids tossing out the wildest, silliest ideas they can think of.

Funny thing is, the bad ones often spark the great ones. Give it a shot! #DesignThinking #Brainstorm #ClassroomFun https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XJ01bS3AFic

Want kids to spot what's truly the same and what's not? 🔍 Creative Comparisons is a Project Zero routine that nudges them to look past the surface.

Their thinking gets sharper, their writing gets clearer.

Watch it in action! #ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines #ClassroomTips https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XtrFytWtEZA

How do you teach grit without the lecture? 💪 Meet the Perseverance Coach.

It's a tool that helps kids work through hard tasks step by step, so they keep going when things get tough.

Less giving up, more growing! #GrowthMindset #Grit #StudentSuccess https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1aQpC0knEKo

Want kids to design with real care for others? 💛 Interview for Empathy is a d.school move that teaches them how to ask, listen, and learn from the folks they're trying to help.

Stronger interviews mean better ideas.

Watch how it plays out! #DesignThinking #Empathy #StudentCentered https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lMj8f1gs6j4

Want your kids to fall in love with poems? ✏️ Poetry-Lab turns writing into a low-stakes, high-fun playground.

Kids try out forms, voice, and word choices without fear of getting it wrong.

It's the kind of space where real writers grow. Check the video! #ELA #PoetryUnit #WritingClass https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mcERwaFpTIY

Ever wish you could turn tough choices into a learning game? 🎮 Decision Quest does just that.

Kids walk through real-world stories and weigh their picks, building thinking skills they'll use forever.

Such a fun way to teach choice and outcome. Check it out! #EdTech #LearningGames #StudentVoice https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sTerx6YxRVw

Tired of feedback that goes nowhere?

Try a Feedback Capture Grid. It's a simple four-square sheet!

What I like. What I'd change. Questions I have. Ideas it sparked.

Kids fill it out after a peer share. Teachers use it after lessons too.

It turns weak feedback into useful gold ✨

https://youtu.be/kyI2iDf3HUA

#FeedbackTools #DesignThinking #Teachers

Want kids to think before they trust? 🚦 Red Light, Yellow Light helps them spot when to pause and when to dig deeper.

It's a Project Zero routine that builds sharp thinkers who don't fall for the first thing they see.

Watch how it works in real classrooms! #ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines #VisibleThinking https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eIrmgqc5vk4

What helps a class grow more, big units or tiny daily check-ins?

I used to skip the small stuff. Then I tried daily reflection.

Two minutes at the end of class. One question. That's it.

The shift was wild. Kids started owning their thinking out loud!

If you want a simple way to build a thinking habit, start here 💭

https://youtu.be/Iw8t_WMsKwA

#TeacherLife #ReflectivePractice #DesignThinking

column3: Walk Into Office Hours With a Plan
column7:
Office hours sound great in theory. In real life, they're chaos.

Here's what fixed it for me. Walk in with a plan!

Pick three things you want to cover. Put them on the board. Let students sign up.

Now your time isn't wasted, and kids don't feel rushed.

Save this for the next round 📌

https://youtu.be/aZTQJ8iq5w8

#TeacherTips #OfficeHours #ClassroomManagement

column3: ETLA Tool Evaluation Rubric (Based on ISTE Coaching Standard 4.3)
column7:
How do you know if a tech tool is really worth your time?

The ETLA rubric (built on ISTE Coaching Standard 4.3) gives you a quick way to size up any new tool before you bring it to class.

Save this one for the next time a vendor pitches you something shiny! ✨

Watch: https://youtu.be/dpKqNDLkZDY

#EdTech #ISTE #Coaching

Picture this: it's the last week of class, and your students are hyped instead of checked out.

That's what happens when you wrap up the year like Spotify wraps up a year of music. 🎧

Learning Wrapped helps kids look back at their wins, their growth, and their favorite moments. It's a fun way to close strong!

Watch how it works: https://youtu.be/OKO9Gn5QwGo

#TeacherLife #EndOfYear #SchoolAI

Think Pair Share gets a bad rap.

Most of the time it turns into 'silent think, awkward pair, one kid shares.'

Here's a small tweak that flips it. Set a timer and give each partner 30 seconds to talk. No more, no less.

Try it Monday and tell me how it goes! 💬

Watch: https://youtu.be/2z577ZeHtxM

#TeacherTips #Discussion #SchoolAI

Treasure Island hits different when kids ask 'what does this guy really want?'

This SchoolAI coach helps Grade 5 readers dig into why each character does what they do. No more surface reads.

It's the kind of close reading that sticks! 📖

See it in action: https://youtu.be/d4-9zWoaaCM

#CKLA #5thGrade #Reading

Want kids to slow down and really look? 👀

The AEIOU lab walks them through five lenses: actions, environment, things, users, and what's said. Each lens turns into notes.

It's the kind of mini tool teachers can pull out for any field trip, video, or even a hallway walk.

Save the demo for next time!
https://youtu.be/Bo5p31PDL1s

You don't peel a banana from the bottom.

Same goes for tough topics in class. Most kids start with the obvious stuff and stop there.

Peel the Fruit (a Project Zero routine) walks them deeper, layer by layer, until they hit the core idea. So good! 🍌

See how to run it: https://youtu.be/nk6k3h7VaBU

#ProjectZero #Thinking #ClassroomRoutines

Books can be windows. Books can be mirrors. Sometimes they're both.

When kids see themselves in a story, they read closer. When they see new lives, they grow. That's the whole point!

Here's how to bring this into ELA 🪞

https://youtu.be/Os15b4M_dgY

Ever hit that 2pm wall with your students?

The Re-Energize Card is your reset button. Students pick a card, do a quick move, and the whole room snaps back to focus.

Tiny shift, big payoff. ⚡

Watch the magic here: https://youtu.be/wvlz4-pMkNc

#TeacherLife #SEL #ClassroomReset

Ever pulled a poem out of a piece of art? 🎨

That's the heart of the Soundsuits Found Poem space. Kids look at art, grab words that pull them in, then shape those words into a poem of their own.

It works because the art does the heavy lift. Kids stop worrying about a blank page and start playing with words.

Watch how it runs!
https://youtu.be/V0xrRkTNBEc

Forget the boring "All About Me" worksheet.

Identity Maps with a Twist lets kids draw who they are with symbols and shapes. By day three you'll know your class better than month one of last year.

Real bonds in one lesson. 🗺️

See it in action: https://youtu.be/EvhJklJB8j4

#BackToSchool #GetToKnowYou #TeacherTips

Langston Hughes wrote "I, Too" back in 1926. Kids still feel its punch today!

Use it as a poem starter. Have students write their own "I, too..." line about who they are and where they belong.

Here's the full move ✍️

https://youtu.be/Kz73_uc3VL0

Most lessons end in a packing-up rush. Try ending with a poem.

Kids write three lines about what they learned, what they wonder, or how they feel. It's quick. It's calm. It sticks!

Watch it in action 📝

https://youtu.be/1cM3_i0OSq8

My class wrote a poem on day two of school.

Each kid added one line about who we are. By the end, we had something that felt like home.

Now it lives on our wall. Every kid sees their voice in it. 💛

Try Our Community Poem with your class: https://youtu.be/Wwrk7d0AaIw

#BackToSchool #ELA #ClassCulture

Picture books aren't just for little kids. They're a smart way to teach honest history at any grade!

You get short text, strong art, and room to talk. Kids dig into hard topics with care.

Here's how to run one well 📖

https://youtu.be/DvkIlTa5pyg

Quick win for any teacher who loves design thinking 💡

Run a 10-minute Empathy Interview Sprint. Students partner up, ask open questions, then listen.

You'll see the room shift. Promise.
https://youtu.be/Rx5ep8oHdfo
#DesignThinking #EmpathyInClass

Read-alouds don't have to feel flat.

Stop on one word. Show the picture. Let kids guess what comes next. Your voice changes the whole story.

Kids lean in when you make space for wonder. 📖

Watch the Artful Read-Aloud move: https://youtu.be/HfxN3q9EFxE

#ELA #ReadAloud #TeacherLife

Save this for your next cultural month.

Pick one figure, one song, and one tradition. Let kids dig in and share what they find. Done in three days.

Skip the worksheet. Make it feel real. 🌍

Cultural Month Spotlight here: https://youtu.be/3mPkQiNtELQ

#TeacherTips #SocialStudies #CulturalMonth

Save this one for your next lesson plan.

Look to the Stars is low prep, high pull, and lands fast. Pin it now so you have it when you need it!

See how it plays out 📌

https://youtu.be/NVaUzE9fir4

Save this one for your next reading lesson 📌

Sentence-Phrase-Word: students pick the line, phrase, and word that hit hardest from a text.

Then they share. The chat writes itself.
https://youtu.be/fGuYY4i2_VI
#ReadingStrategies #ProjectZero

Three quotes. One source. Big talk 🎯

That's the setup for Three-Quote Source Talks. Students grab three lines from a source, share why each one matters, and listen for what classmates picked.

Reading turns into a real chat fast.
https://youtu.be/i6kLymZ8xWg
#ELAStrategies #ReadingComprehension

Turn-and-talks fall flat without good stems. So fix that 💬

The Sentence Stem Studio gives kids real frames to start with. Things like 'I agree because' or 'I'd push back on'.

Print one set, use them all year.
https://youtu.be/3P3zV0YSdgU
#TeacherStrategies #ELA

Want kids who care about what they read? 💭

Try Project Zero's THINK, FEEL, CARE routine.

Pick a person, place, or part of a system. Ask what they think, feel, and care about.

It builds real empathy. Watch how it works.
https://youtu.be/gxgFn6djWOg
#TeacherTips #ProjectZero #ThinkingRoutines

What if Mentor Poem Writing was the one move that shifted your week?

It's quick, it's clear, and it gives kids something to chew on. No big lift. Big payoff!

See how it plays out ✨

https://youtu.be/e4lI6iih4Lw

What if the best lesson plan is just one good question?

Wonder is the spark that makes kids lean in. It's free. It's quick. And it works every time!

Here's a simple way to spark it 🌱

https://youtu.be/Gyo5blP3Z6c

Why-How Laddering is a tiny tool that builds big thinkers.

Ask "why?" to climb up to the heart of an idea. Ask "how?" to climb down to the steps that make it real. Kids see the whole picture!

It's a Stanford d.school move. Try it 🪜

https://youtu.be/fcFpMOi3bAM

Word problems freak kids out. They don't need to.

Try a Word Problem Translator. Kids tell the story in their own words first, then turn it into math. The fog lifts fast!

Watch how it works 📐

https://youtu.be/32SuDfucNWc

You want every kid to feel seen on day one. Here's how.

Kids sketch a self-portrait. Then each one joins a class mural. The room turns into a map of who's here!

It sets the whole year in a great way 🎨

https://youtu.be/pAkky87WFC0

Your students walk in wondering if they fit.

That tiny worry shapes the whole day. The Belonging Lab is a quick set of moves that tells every kid "you're seen here."

Your room shifts in days, not months. ✨

See how to set it up: https://youtu.be/dEHCUIQjUow

#TeacherTips #ClassCulture #BelongingMatters

Picture this. Your loudest student passes a card to your quietest one. They both grin 🤫

That's a Whisper Card moment. A tiny prompt that shifts who talks, who listens, and who gets seen.

Try it today.
https://youtu.be/8j4dv_gdMuQ
#ClassroomStrategies #StudentVoice

Every classroom has stories your kids never got to share. Hidden Histories is a low-prep way to wrap the year by surfacing the moments that mattered to them most. 📖
Watch the walkthrough: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=walhZ79Ndr4

One letter. One year. One chance for your students to look back and see how far they came. The End-of-Year Letter Space helps them reflect with heart, not hashtags. 💌
See how it works: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iwg_2PLurqk

Pin this for the last week. Last Day of School Stations gives you five ready-to-go rotations so the final day feels meaningful, not chaotic. 📌
Save this one: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VK57zf1IwR0

Project Zero's Hot Spots routine is one of the smartest ways to help kids notice what's missing in a text, image, or moment. It's a quiet skill that pays off all year. 🔥
Watch it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9YdKE0557xI

Some books end with a whisper. Some end with a punch. Famous Last Lines Countdown lets your kids rank the closers that hit hardest, then write their own. 📚
Take a look: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VEYlwdC2kJo

The 5 Why's looks simple on paper. In a classroom, it cracks open the why behind any problem your students are trying to solve. 🧠
See it in action: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Q3KFmX4PCU

Turn the last days of school into a memory worth keeping. Synthesis Time Capsule asks students to bottle up what they learned, what they loved, and what they want next year's kids to know. 🎁
Watch it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=00hu_fjF75c

What's the last line you want your students to remember? Famous Last Lines Countdown turns the final week into a party of voice, growth, and the words that stick. 🎤
Check it out: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oTGrAd3sjPc

You're tired. Your kids are tired. Burn Bright is a closing activity that helps everyone leave the year feeling lit up instead of burned out. ✨
Take a peek: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vfYvsah7PCQ

Tiny shifts, big change. Powers of 10 helps kids zoom in on the small stuff that makes a project work, then zoom out to see the whole picture. It's a fast way to spark fresh thinking on any unit. 🔍
Watch it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2FwEI2yYMXo

Got a story to teach? Here's a Project Zero thinking routine I love.

Beginning, Middle, End helps kids slow down and notice the shape of any story or topic.

It works for books, art, science, even social moments. Real flexible.

Try it tomorrow with your class 📖

https://youtu.be/MugFQR5Rh5c

Want a quick warm-up that sparks creative thinking?

Hand out a paper with 30 blank circles and 3 minutes on the clock.

Kids turn each circle into something new. Sun, eye, smiley, wheel.

Easy, fun, and you'll see who thinks fast and who plays it safe ✏️

https://youtu.be/QSJHjqCFovM

What if you mashed up your three favorite students into one person? That's the Composite Character Profile. It's a design thinking move that helps you spot real needs, not just guesses. Watch how it works and try it in your next planning meeting. 🎯

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CzWBLu-3sdc

"True for who?" is a tiny question with huge power.

Whose voice gets to call something true in your room?

This Project Zero routine helps kids see how truth shifts when you change the lens. It's perfect for tough text talks or current events.

Try it once and watch the room open up.

Watch it here: https://youtu.be/t2l5kYCZKEE 🤔

Ever finish a week and wonder where it went?

Walk the Week is a quick reflection routine that lets kids look back at the highs, lows, and aha moments before the bell rings Friday.

It takes ten minutes. The payoff? Real student voice and clear next steps.

Watch how it works: https://youtu.be/6T8KQ8-g-Qo 🚶

Want to know what your kids are really thinking?

Try the 3-2-1 Bridge! Three ideas, two questions, one image before a lesson. Then run it again after.

The shift between the two is where the magic shows up 🌉

Watch the quick how-to: https://youtu.be/tVDnrqz0HDo

You know that one kid who quietly shapes the whole room? A Stakeholder Map helps you see them and everyone else tied to your next move. 🗺️ Jot down each person, what they want, and what they fear. You'll spot blind spots fast, and your plan gets way sharper. Try it before a tough call! https://youtu.be/kF_RN6X5yhQ

Ever notice how kids will stare at a photo and then say something wild? That's not luck. That's Thinking with Images at work. 🖼️ Show them one strong image, ask what they see, then what it makes them think. You'll get ideas you didn't plan for, and quiet kids find their voice. It's the kind of move that turns a flat lesson into a real one! https://youtu.be/ZaC6q4jT67Q

column3: Take a Safari Walk With One Word
column7: What if one word could turn a reading block into a safari? That's the move here. 🦁 Pick a word, send the kids hunting for it in a book, on a wall, or out the window. They circle, count, and share. Suddenly that one small word feels huge, and the room is buzzing. Reading muscles get a real workout, no worksheet in sight! https://youtu.be/cbDgWVZ5GbE

column3: Star the Story Before and After
column7: Save this one for any ELA week. ⭐ Have kids star three things in a story before they read, then star three after. The gap between those two lists is gold. They'll spot how their thinking shifted, and you'll spot where they got stuck. It's small, fast, and works for any grade. Quick to plan, big payoff! https://youtu.be/53t8Eb2ZNnU

Check out Four Corners. This is a fun class move that gets students up and moving to share what they think. You pick a corner of the room based on if you agree, sort of agree, sort of don't, or don't at all. It's a great way to hear from every voice and start good talks! 💬

Dive into HumanVsAI. This video shows how humans and AI are the same and how they're not. You'll learn what each does well and what each is still learning. It's a great chance to think about how new tech is changing things and what it means for us! 🤖

What is this? A fun guessing game that gets minds moving! You look at a close-up photo and try to guess what it is. You'll be amazed at how tricky it can be when you can't see the whole thing. Great for building focus and sharp thinking skills! 🔍

What happens next? This video teaches you to predict what comes after what you're seeing. You look at a scene and guess what will happen next. It helps you think ahead and use what you know to make smart guesses about the future. Great for building thinking skills! 🔮

Which one doesn't belong? Look at four items and pick the one that's not like the others. You'll need to think about what makes things the same and what makes them not fit. This builds your brain's power to spot patterns and think deep. A great warm-up for any class! 🎯

Class vs. Teacher. What's the one big thing that the class sees or does that the teacher doesn't? This video helps you spot the gap between how things look and what's really going on. It builds sharp eyes and clear minds! 🙏 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S-3noWKi_8o

Real problem. Sixty seconds. You get a real-world mess and just one minute to dream up a fix. It's fast, it's fun, and it gets your brain moving quick. Great for showing that good ideas can come fast when you trust your mind! ⚡

Finding Evidence. Make a claim and then hunt for proof that backs it up. This video shows you how to be a thought detective. You'll learn to spot what's real and what's just a guess. Great for strong reading and clear thinking! 🔎

Multiple Perspectives. The same event looks different to every person who sees it. This video helps you get into other people's shoes and see their view of the world. You'll grow your sense of what it means to be fair and kind to everyone! 👥 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wk5uLWG6lGU

Ever taught the water cycle and felt your students zone out? The Frog Cycle flips the script. Instead of diagrams and vocab lists, kids become the frogs moving through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation. Hands-on, memorable, and way less boring than textbooks. Your next unit is here

Your kids hit a problem and freeze. They don't know where to start. Problem Solve Your Way walks them through it—break it down, brainstorm options, test ideas, learn from fails. It's not about getting it right fast. It's about thinking like someone who solves stuff. That's the real skill

Theme detective work trains kids to spot the big idea hiding in the details. What lesson keeps showing up? What's the author really trying to say? THEME DETECTIVES makes that thinking visible and concrete. Your students stop just reading and start *understanding*

Short vowels trip up so many readers. This resource breaks them down—here's the sound, here's how your mouth moves, here's words that have it. Not just drills. Real teaching. SHORT VOWEL DETECTIVES helps kids build the sound patterns that make fluency click

Here's how you teach central ideas without making it painful. Kids read an exemplar, see where the main idea lives, then hunt for it in their own text. CENTRAL IDEA HUNT shows them the thinking, not just the answer. They learn how to find the heartbeat of any passage

One good question can change a whole unit. THE QUESTION LAB helps you craft questions that make kids think, not just recall. Questions that open doors instead of shutting them. Questions your students will actually *want* to explore

Food webs confuse kids. Iron Chef Food Web fixes it. By cooking, tasting, competing, they *see* how energy moves through systems. No abstract arrows. Just real stakes, real learning. Your next ecology unit writes itself

Chunk and Find is the cheat code for teaching students to manage info overload. Find the key stuff. Chunk it. Remember it. Repeat. It works for any subject, any text, any test prep. Your kids will use this for the rest of school

Your students will love Cell Safari. This science resource turns cell exploring into an adventure where they find real structures and ask smart questions. They'll understand how cells work in ways that stick. Try it! 🔬
https://youtu.be/rCyvsV1lHUM

The 5 E model turns science class into real work. Your kids Engage with a real question, Explore it hands-on, Explain what they find, Elab on it with new ideas, and Eval all of it. Five steps that take science from just facts to real learning. That's how kids get it. 🔬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iq8f3IfUyg

Feed back that helps kids grow. That's what A Discover Feed back Activity is all about. Instead of just being told what went wrong, your kids find out what went right and what could be better.
